steps.path: Review ticket → Optional AI help → Let your assistant try to fix it → Start
steps.headline: When does "Downloading YouCoded's code" happen, and should the ticket screen offer it at all?

options.label: Remove from tickets
pros: The ticket screen is only about reporting — nothing surprising for everyday users
No hidden download of about 1 GB, and no pile of copies
Help & feedback → Contribute still offers working on YouCoded's code, with its own explanation
cons: Someone who wants the assistant to fix a bug takes one more step (Contribute)
options.cost: Small: the row and its two waiting/failed screens go.

options.label: Keep, download once
pros: The row says up front it downloads about 1 GB the first time
Later uses start straight away, reusing the copy on your computer
cons: Still a developer action on a screen everyone uses
The 1 GB download still surprises people the first time
options.cost: A change to how the app finds its earlier download, plus new wording.

options.label: Hand over to Contribute
pros: One place explains and sets up the download (Contribute)
Your ticket's words are carried over, so you don't retype them
cons: Contribute itself also downloads a fresh copy each time today, so that needs the same fix
options.cost: Medium: a new hand-off between the two popups.

steps.today: You reach this only by choosing Review ticket → Optional AI help → "Let your assistant try to fix it" → Start. It downloads YouCoded's own code (about 1 GB, by the app's own note) into a folder on your computer, then opens a new conversation that works on a fix. Nothing is sent to GitHub.
steps.problem: It happens again after every restart of the app: the app forgets the earlier download and makes a new copy each time (youcoded-workspace, -2, -3…). The screen says "a few minutes the first time", which isn't true. And on a screen for reporting a problem, a code download makes little sense to someone who isn't a developer.
steps.proposal: Pick what this screen should do with it. Nothing has changed yet. Round 2's failed-download screen (ST2-9) goes with whatever you pick.
